rationale: A considered-and-cleared note that asserts no defect; the instant path sets interval 1 and every evaluator that reaches this line derives a non-zero interval, so nothing is actionable.

The new counter is two lines of wiring that mirror querySamples, which itself has no registration or accumulation test anywhere in the repo; the underlying SamplesRead value is heavily asserted in engine_test.go.
Considered-and-cleared performance note; totalHPointSize was already computed once per step at the old IncrementSamplesAtStep call site, so it asserts no defect.
metrics.querySamplesRead appears exactly once in the single opts.Reg.MustRegister call; there is no second registration path in NewEngine.

The clamp is exercised: for max_over_time(metricWith3SampleEvery10Seconds[60s:5s]) start=201 end=220 step=5 the child step at t=220000 yields outerStep 4 against numOuterSteps 4, which is why engine_test.go:1432 expects 216000: 9 with the comment 'steps after last outer'.

The SubqueryExpr case mutates ev.samplesStats.SamplesRead and SamplesReadPerStep directly while util/stats/query_stats.go:423-433 exposes MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery for the same job, so two different merge semantics for subquery reads now live in two packages.

The parent stats are swapped in and restored without defer, so a panic from ev.error inside ev.eval leaves the child installed and skips the merge; impact is limited because the query aborts, but the counter under-reports on that path.

The ceiling expression maps a child step tk to the first outer step at or after tk, which is the intended attribution; tk-start of 1 and of exactly one interval both land on step 1, so there is no off-by-one in the formula itself.

True that neither caller passes nil, but the nil receiver guard is the established idiom throughout this file (IncrementSamplesAtStep, UpdatePeak, MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery); removing it would break the convention rather than fix anything.

The buffer-reuse branch is reachable via at-modifier-unsafe range functions such as predict_linear(foo[5m] @ T, y) in a range query, and no test in TestQueryStatistics covers that shape, so the TotalSamples change on that branch is unguarded by tests.
The cluster itself concedes no asymmetric call can be constructed; parent and child are both built from the same EnablePerStepStats flag, so the slices are either both nil or both allocated.

IncrementSamplesReadAtStep checks only i < len while IncrementSamplesReadAtTimestamp at line 364 also checks i >= 0; the asymmetry is real and cheap to fix, though no current caller passes a negative index.

evalSubquery merges the child's SamplesRead and the range-vector loop then counts the same materialized matrix points again at line 2184; this is exactly the doubling the reviewer challenges at engine_test.go:1551, where the test asserts SamplesRead 2 with the comment 'subquery + outer' and the reviewer argues it should be 1.

SamplesReadPerStepMap does return *TotalSamplesPerStep, but that type is a generic timestamp-to-count map already reused as the per-step container; the objection is naming only, with no behavioral consequence.

Same defect the reviewer raises at util/stats/query_stats.go:432: the subquery-to-parent per-step attribution does not reflect real step windows, collapsing pre-window child steps onto step 0 and clamping steps past the last outer step onto the final one.

QuerySamples is per-query state mutated only by the single evaluation goroutine (no goroutine is spawned anywhere in promql/engine.go), and the new fields are accessed exactly like the pre-existing TotalSamples fields, so no new concurrency hazard is introduced.

The StepInvariantExpr child is still built with NewChild(), which forces per-step stats off, while every other new child uses NewChildWithStepTracking; the resulting all-at-step-0 attribution is defensible for a once-evaluated subtree but the asymmetry against the duplicated TotalSamples loop directly above deserves justification.
CHANGELOG.md in this repo is organized by released version with no unreleased section (top entry is 3.10.0), so entries are added at release time rather than per PR.

fullWindowCount is declared zero at line 2145 and assigned only inside the ts == startTimestamp || Timestamp == nil branch, so on an @-modifier buffer-reuse step IncrementSamplesAtStep now adds 0 where the old unconditional call added the retained window; reachable via at-modifier-unsafe range functions (predict_linear), and it silently changes totalQueryableSamples and prometheus_engine_query_samples_total despite the comment claiming unchanged semantics.

The shipped IMPLEMENTATION NOTES banner, including the line admitting 'some sample count calculations may need refinement based on actual query execution', is precisely the block the reviewer says should not be here, and the surrounding expectations carry comments like 'Actual behavior' and 'corrected values' showing they were read off the implementation.
